hints.title: Wiggle Order Eliminates Averages
hints.text: If every element is either strictly greater than both neighbors or strictly less than both neighbors, it can never equal their average.

hints.title: Sorting and Alternating High-Low Halves
hints.text: Sort the array, then interleave elements from the smaller half with elements from the larger half.

hints.title: Placing Elements into Alternating Slots
hints.text: Populate even indices with the smaller sorted numbers and odd indices with the larger sorted numbers.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def rearrangeArray(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        nums.sort()
        ans = [0] * len(nums)
        ans[::2] = nums[: (len(nums) + 1) // 2]
        ans[1::2] = nums[(len(nums) + 1) // 2 :]
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by high-low parity interleaving.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Random shuffling or local swapping can get stuck in permutation cycles.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Wiggle sorting guarantees the peak-valley condition everywhere.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that making elements alternating local peaks and valleys guarantees no element equals its neighbors average.
